title: Prove the sharp mixed-quadratic inverse factor two (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

For a quadratic with exactly one root inside and one outside the unit circle, prove the sharp inverse bound

```text
P(z) = c(z-a)(1-bz), |a|<1, 0<|b|<1
m = min(|a|,|b|), delta = min_{|z|=1}|P(z)|
delta ||1/P||_W <= (1+m)^2/(1+m^2) < 2
```

Claim type: scoped proof with exact finite corroboration. The same optimal factors bound `||P(tau Z_L^w)^(-1)||_infinity`, uniformly over cyclic length, integer stride and unit phase. The radius-dependent factor is attained by `a=r,b=-r`; the least uniform factor is two. This replaces #803's general degree-two sufficient multiplier 81 on the stated mixed-root subclass. No new kappa is claimed.

Add only `research/mixed-quadratic-circle-bound/`. This contribution is produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Rafael Guevara #803 for the general bound and its nonoptimality question, Ali Romman #621 for the cyclic setting, Thiago Costa #802 for Fourier-transfer work and Ryan Pinto #692 for the retained geometric-resolvent lineage. The proof uses classical geometric-series and Fourier methods and makes no literature-priority claim for them. Predecessor results are cited premises, without importing or replaying their executables.

## Evidence

Before: #803 gives `(1+4n)^2/delta`, hence `81/delta` at degree two, without an optimal degree factor. After: `PROOF.md` gives the exact two-sided Laurent norm, the sharp radius-sensitive inequality, uniform factor two, and cyclic sharpness by coefficient folding as length grows.

Local CPython 3.12.15 checks passed:

- 192 exact endpoint inequalities; 768 dense-elimination versus finite-geometric inverse comparisons, covering 2,688 entries and 192 antipodal exact-gap cases; 63 rational sharpness identities; eight semantic controls.
- Registered warning-strict ordinary and optimized commands, and direct standalone execution. Each registered command took under one second locally; this is timeout evidence, not a performance claim.
- Generated source-bound receipt replay; altered count, Boolean type, source hashes and duplicate JSON keys reject. Exclusive-create rejects overwrite while preserving the receipt. An actual proof-byte mutation in the exported copy rejects against its pre-mutation receipt.
- Metadata/pins, exact committed bytes and source history, official export/integrity and Git-free optimized replay pass at `6022a32a01cf8bdc19d382fa1a657ecd4afada14`.

A reviewer can substitute their CPython 3.12 executable. Replay uses only the standard library and writes nothing by default. `--emit-to NEW_EXTERNAL_FILE` creates an optional generated receipt, and `--check-receipt FILE` recomputes the result and all six source hashes. Historical source pins are at canonical main `624de9dc66858af0945e5f8a0942488d62280d43`, priority revision 7. Full-main, merged-PR, live PR and Discussion overlap searches were refreshed before committing; sparse notes, arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits.

## Limitations

The universal quantifiers rest on the written proof. Finite enumeration does not exhaust complex roots. The bound concerns exact mixed quadratic operators, not the general arbitrary-degree case. Coefficient preparation, rounded execution, dirty restoration, fixed-tape costs, complete caller invoices and supplier admission remain open. No selected-frontier change or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No Lean, Docker or full selected cold replay was run, and no proof obligation was deferred solely to CI.

## Open next questions

- Determine the optimal multiplier for quadratics with both roots outside the circle, starting with separated two-pole phases. Coefficient cancellation blocks the present disjoint-series argument.
- Identify one actual mixed-quadratic caller and carry this bound through its complete rounding recurrence, including preparation, every prefix and restoration.

## Related open work

No open PR on the same sharp mixed-quadratic Wiener multiplier was found in the inspected coverage. Nearby cyclic-inverse work includes:

- #4908 implements phase-preserving cyclic recovery with bounded-word rounding for a linear observation operator. This PR proves a sharp exact norm inequality for a mixed quadratic, and does not supply that physical implementation.
- #4842 studies complete observation-cascade Euclidean conditioning. This PR studies Laurent coefficient norms and induced infinity norms for scalar quadratic cyclic polynomials; no common numerical invariant is compared.

The completion refresh read this account's nine other open PRs created since the CLAIM: #4909, #4910, #4911, #4912, #4915, #4916, #4917, #4918 and #4919. They study query capacity, tensor-error dimension, a fixed source-basis walk, square-zero call compilation, idempotent orbit counts, ring-valued fanout, a full-mask rank, signed unitriangular tariffs and shared subspace maps. None studies this mixed-quadratic Wiener multiplier or reports a competing value for it. No additional computations were run to compare their results.
